newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice scores new contract highs on weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice scores new contract highs on weather.

text.p: Weather concerns and heavy commodity fund buying pushed CBOT rice futures to a higher close and contract highs Thursday, traders and analysts said.

"There's legitimate weather concerns," said Jack Scoville, analyst with the Price Group brokerage in Chicago. "If this El Nino does do anything, it will hit rice producing areas in India, the North China plains and the Philippines."
For the second consecutive session, all months except July made new contract highs.
Traders continue to monitor the building El Nino weather pattern, which could bring drought to many areas.
Advances were limited late by heavy hedge selling from farmers, millers and elevators, pit traders said.
As rice prices continue to climb, speculative interest in the market is growing, traders said.
"You've got only one bull market going on on this (trading) floor, and it's rice," said one trader.
Volume over the past two days has been building and is near the past record of 2,775 set on February 5, 1997. Traders estimated volume Thursday at 2,000 lots.
Rice closed seven to 10 cents per cwt higher, with July up eight at $11.75 per cwt.
